The treated effluent was to be used for irrigation purposes, however farmers and land owners are unwilling to use the high TDS effluent due to developed irrigation facility in this area by Narmada Water Resources, Water Supply & Kalpsar Department (NWRWS&KD-Irrigation Department, Government of Gujarat). Hence, it is proposed to dispose the treated effluent (to be collected from existing CETPs at Jetpur, Bhat Gam and from the proposed CETP at Manpar Derdi) into deep sea through pipeline.

The max. peak demand observed is 150 MW with an average max. demand of 130 MW indicating a very high diversity factor.

Project Description:
GHCL Sutrapada is presently discharging combined treated effluent of 16000 m3/hr through two separate outfall pipelines, each carrying 8000 m3/hr. The combined treated effluent consists of treated effluent from soda ash plant and cooling water.
-The Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) has proposed to develop a fishing harbour in the vicinity of GHCL existing outfall location. In this connection GMB has asked GHCL to shift the outfall locations slightly away from the proposed harbour. 

- Due to the COVID restriction and subsequent lockdown, the manufacturing plant was temporarily shut down resulting in choking in one of the outfall pipelines caused by deposition of marine sediments from the outfall point. 

Hence, the outfall point of the proposed outfall pipeline will be located far away from the proposed fishing harbour for future sustainability of the plant.
After the laying of the new pipeline, the old two pipelines will be non operational.

The Motaraypura Pumped Storage Project, with a planned capacity of 1,000 MW, is proposed by the Gujarat State Electricity Corporation Limited (GSECL) in Nandod Taluka, Narmada District, Gujarat. The project site is located adjacent to the Karjan Reservoir, near Jitgadh Village, within Nandod Taluka, Narmada District. Geographically, the project area lies between latitude 21°48’11” N to 21°49’23” N and longitude 73°32’55” E to 73°35’01” E.
The project will be situated between the newly constructed upper reservoir and the existing Karjan Dam, which will function as the lower reservoir. Designed to generate 1,000 MW of power, it will operate under an approximate head of 170 meters.
The two reservoirs will be interconnected through an underground water conductor system consisting of a Head Race Tunnel, Surge Shaft, steel-lined Pressure Shafts, an Underground Powerhouse with a Transformer Cavern, and a Tail Race Tunnel.

Project Description: KIRI INFRASTRUCTURE PVT. LTD proposes the construction of  captive jetty near Jafarabad, Amreli District, Gujarat, with a handling capacity of  4.98 MMTPA. The jetty will facilitate unloading of bulk and liquid cargo, including Ammonia, Sulphuric Acid, and Phosphoric Acid, to support the Copper and Fertilizer Plant of IACL and IAFL. The project  includes an offshore breakwater for wave protection. The jetty will avoid dredging of the seabed and include provisions for future expansion.  KIPL plans to establish  100 MLD desalination plant to ensure a reliable water supply for the project. An integrated seawater intake and outfall system will be constructed, with intake pipelines and an offshore pump house based on an approach trestle concept to secure continuous seawater availability. The reject brine will be discharged through  diffusers via outfall pipelines. Cargo will be conveyed from  jetty to Copper and Fertilizer Plant via a 15.2 km pipe rack conveyor from the backup area.
Project Name: Construction of Captive Jetty (4.98 MMTPA) with Bulk and Liquid Cargo Handling and Transport Facilities, and 100 MLD Desalination Plant with Associated Marine and Onshore Infrastructure for KIRI INFRASTRUCTURE PVT. LTD., Amreli District, Gujarat

Project Description:
The proposed project starts from Km 264+500 near the Junction of SH-7 (village Khirai) in Morbi district and terminated at Km 306+250 near the Junction with NH-41 (Samakhiyali) in Kutchh District of Gujarat. This section of NH 27 in Gujarat is strategically connected to major ports like Deendayal (Kandla) Port, Mundra, Gandhidham on North side with important logistics hub for industries in Morbi, Jamnagar, Navlakhia port and surrounding regions. Project Description:
Currently, the unit is operational with Natural Gas based boilers. Out of total 6 boilers (7 TPH, 8 TPH, 15 TPH, 18 TPH, 30 TPH and 30 TPH) installed at premises, different boilers are operated at different point of time as per requirement of steam in manufacturing various products.
The NG supplier GAIL (due to Geopolitical issue), has curtailed the gas commitment by 40 % and the NG is also used as RM (which cannot be substituted), so availability of NG as fuel is reduced largely.  Considering this, PP is constrained to switch to alternate fuel.
Now, looking at various aspects including steam continuity and pressure, GACL intends to install two solid fuel fired boiler of 25 TPH each. It is proposed to use coal and bio-fuel as per suitability/availability. Once new solid fuel fired boilers come in to operation, 3 Nos. of natural gas-based boilers (i.e. 15 TPH, 8 TPH and 30 TPH) will be removed and rest of natural gas-based boilers will become stand-by (i.e. 18 TPH, 7 TPH and 30 TPH).
